info.title: HorecaOS Platform API

get.summary: List failed inbox messages for one consumer

get.description: Keyed by consumer and event together, because one event reaches several consumers and each has its own attempt count and its own decision. The payload is never returned (ADR 0029); tenantId narrows the read and a message outside it is reported as not found, never as forbidden.
get.summary: Inspect one consumer's copy of one event

post.summary: Declare that an inbox message needs no further processing
Return a dead-lettered inbox message to pending for one consumer

get.summary: List failed outbox events

get.description: The routing, retry, and resolution facts of a single event. The payload is never returned: working the failure queue is not authority to read the customer record behind an item (ADR 0029). tenantId narrows the read exactly as it narrows the list; an event outside it is reported as not found, never as forbidden.
get.summary: Inspect one outbox event

post.description: Irreversible. Uncertain provider outcomes require reconciliation evidence and a second approver.
post.summary: Declare that an outbox event needs no further processing

post.description: Retries the same immutable event; it never mints a new event id.
post.summary: Return a dead-lettered outbox event to pending

get.description: Only activated versions. A draft is an unfinished commercial decision and showing one invites somebody to quote it.
get.summary: The activated plan catalogue

post.description: Requires the global platform-admin role.
post.summary: Create a provisioning tenant

get.description: Requires platform access or membership in the tenant organization.
get.summary: Get a tenant

get.description: Every version of each policy, newest first. An action code with no row here needs no second signature, which is the state every action is in until somebody publishes one.
get.summary: List the approval policies governing this tenant

post.description: Never an edit. The previous open version is closed at the instant this one starts, so what an earlier approver was shown stays readable and the version snapshotted onto their request still means what it said.
post.summary: Publish the next version of an approval policy

get.description: An empty configuredScopes list is an unresolved action. Its missingPolicyMode states whether it currently proceeds on one signature or is refused until a policy is authored. A scoped row is not presented as tenant-wide coverage.
get.summary: Show registered approval actions and their configured scopes

post.description: Closes the version's window, which is the only way to retire a threshold: resolution takes the highest version whose window is open, so a superseding row cannot switch an earlier one off. This is how an operator says stop requiring approval, so it only applies to the version in force. Retroactive ends are refused, a closed version is never reopened — that is a new version — and a version scheduled to take effect later is refused too: cancelling it would leave the version it superseded closed with nothing to follow it, which turns the control off from the scheduled date onwards. To call off a scheduled change, publish the threshold you want as a new version.
post.summary: End-date a policy version

get.description: Oldest first, so the request closest to lapsing is the one on top. Lapsed requests are excluded whether or not the expiry sweep has reached them yet. The maker's free-text reason is deliberately not returned: it is unclassified prose about a named customer (ADR 0029), and the action's own console already holds the detail behind its own capability.
get.summary: List the requests waiting for a second signature

post.description: Refused unless the caller holds the capability the governing policy version named as the second signature, and refused outright if the caller is the person who raised the request. An approval lets the maker's identical resubmission proceed exactly once — executing under it moves the request to CONSUMED, so the next identical submission raises a new request needing a new signature. A decline blocks it with the reason given here. Both refusals and decisions are audited.
post.summary: Approve or decline a pending request

get.description: Reading audit is itself audited. The change document is not returned in a list; retrieving it is a separate, individually audited read.
get.summary: Search audit evidence within a tenant
List brands within a tenant

post.summary: Create a brand within a tenant
Create a draft catalog
Create a category

post.description: Both together, because a product with no variant cannot be published and would only ever be a half-finished state to come back to.
post.summary: Create a product with its default variant

post.description: A rejected publication is still recorded with its report, so "why did publishing fail an hour ago" has an answer.
post.summary: Snapshot, validate, and make live

get.description: Returns stable codes and the entity each one is about, because "a product has no variant" is unactionable without knowing which product.
get.summary: Report every problem without publishing

put.summary: Place a product in a category

put.description: The delivery fee goes out as an ordinary receipt line, never through Payme's shipping block, which carries no code, no package code and no VAT percent. So it needs the same four fields a dish does.
put.summary: Classify a brand's delivery charge

get.description: catalog.md §4.6, the 86 screen's read side: the read counterpart of PUT .../inventory/variants/{variantId}/availability. Gated on inventory.read rather than catalog.read, matching the screen's own denial rule — an actor who can adjust stock but never touches draft authoring still needs this list.
get.summary: One location's sellable variants, with current availability

post.description: A group whose minimum exceeds the number of options it offers is accepted here and rejected at publication, with the entity path.
post.summary: Create a modifier group
Add an option to a modifier group

put.description: A modifier reaches a receipt as its own line. One linked to a sellable variant inherits that variant's classification instead of carrying a second copy that can drift.
put.summary: Classify a modifier option for fiscal purposes
Attach a modifier group to a product

post.summary: Add a further variant to a product

post.description: Republishes an existing snapshot; it never edits history. The channel comes from the publication itself, so a rollback cannot retire one channel's menu and activate another channel's snapshot.
post.summary: Roll back to a previous publication

put.description: ИКПУ/MXIK, package code, fiscal unit and fiscal name. All four are required by Click and Payme alike; publication reports a gap in any of them rather than refusing the menu, while ADR 0038's coverage tooling is still being built.
put.summary: Classify a variant for fiscal purposes

put.description: Takes effect immediately without republishing. Marking a dish sold out must not require re-validating an entire menu.
put.summary: Set whether a location sells a variant

post.description: The lineage only; the numbers live on versions. At most one tariff per brand may be the default, which is the last rung of fee resolution — and there is no rung after it, because a missing rate table and free delivery must never look alike.
post.summary: Register a rate table

post.description: The middle rung of fee resolution: outranked by a zone's own tariff, and outranking the brand default.
post.summary: Bind the rate table to a branch

post.description: Bands must tile [0, maxDistanceMeters) with no gap and no overlap. Overlap is refused by the database on insert; the gap check runs at activation, because it is a property of the whole set. A gap makes 4,700 m unpriceable while 4,600 m and 4,800 m both price fine.
post.summary: Draft a new version of a rate table

post.description: Refuses a band gap, an inverted fee bound, and ROAD distance with no routing binding installed. Every problem is returned at once.
post.summary: Make a rate table version live

get.description: Runs the full resolver with a fixed clock and writes nothing. The returned evidence is the same shape the stored evidence takes, so what is seen before activation is what will be recorded after it.
get.summary: Simulate a fee at a point, a basket, and an instant
List locations for one brand

post.summary: Create a location owned by exactly one brand

put.summary: Record where a location is, and how to reach it

post.description: Draft: nothing in it prices anything until it is activated, so a season's prices can be built during service without moving a live one.
post.summary: Create a draft price book

get.summary: Read a price book and its current version

post.description: Requires If-Match carrying the book's version, so two operators activating at once cannot both win. Quotes already issued are untouched: they carry their own totals and are honoured at the price the customer was shown until they expire.
post.summary: Put a price book in front of customers

put.description: The fallback every location and channel resolves to when nothing more specific applies.
put.summary: Apply a price book to the whole brand

put.description: Outranks a branch book: an aggregator's agreed prices must not depend on which branch fulfils the order.
put.summary: Apply a price book to one sales channel

put.description: Beats the brand book at that branch. Declared at location scope, so the ADR 0025 check also proves the branch is this brand's.
put.summary: Apply a price book to one branch

put.description: Zero is a legitimate price and means the extra is free. A modifier with no price at all refuses the whole cart rather than pricing at zero.
put.summary: Set what a modifier option costs

put.description: Integer minor units, and for UZS a minor unit is a whole som: 50000 is 50,000 som. VAT-inclusive — this is what the customer pays, with the tax extracted from inside it rather than added on top.
put.summary: Set what a variant costs

put.description: Basis points: 1200 is 12%. INCLUSIVE only — the engine extracts tax from the menu price, and an exclusive profile would be stored and then fail every quote the brand takes. Without a profile every cart in the brand refuses with NO_TAX_PROFILE.
put.summary: Set the brand's VAT rate

post.description: Named and reusable, so thirty branches on one Ramadan timetable edit one object. That is the point, and also the accident.
post.summary: Create a named timetable

put.description: A dated exception replaces the weekly rule for its date rather than adding to it: "we close early on the 31st" must not leave the normal evening window in place.
put.summary: Close a date, or give it replacement hours

put.description: A closing time at or before the opening time means the window ends on the following day, so 18:00-02:00 is one row and not two.
put.summary: Replace the weekly windows

post.description: Creates the lineage only. A zone has no geometry until a version is drafted and activated, so registering one changes nothing a customer sees.
post.summary: Register a zone

post.description: A zone with no binding covers nothing. That is the safe direction: a half-configured zone is visibly inert rather than quietly serving the whole brand.
post.summary: Bind the zone to a branch

post.description: Every edit to geometry, priority, tariff binding or threshold is a new version; the live one is never mutated. A payout dispute six weeks later asks whether that address was inside that polygon, and today's geometry cannot answer it. Supply either a circle around a branch or a GeoJSON polygon, never both.
post.summary: Draft a new version of a zone

post.description: Refuses self-intersecting rings, geometry outside the region's box, and an area above the platform maximum — which is what stops an operator drawing a polygon around the country by accident. Every reason is returned at once rather than one attempt at a time.
post.summary: Make a zone version live

get.description: Each entry names the source its value came from — an override, the plan version, a suspension policy, or the code default — and the mode actually in force after the tenant's enforcement ceiling. Support reads this instead of guessing which of four tables applied.
get.summary: Everything the tenant is entitled to, and why
List active grants within a tenant

post.description: A granter may confer only capabilities it already holds, at a scope it already covers. platform-admin is never grantable here.
post.summary: Grant a role at a scope

delete.description: Takes effect immediately; the cached grant is evicted rather than left to expire.

put.description: Idempotently stores the immutable Keycloak organization ID. Requires platform-admin.
put.summary: Reconcile a tenant's Keycloak organization link

get.summary: List installations, without credentials

post.description: The environment is chosen from an approved catalogue; a tenant never supplies a URL, which closes the request-forgery path at the model.
post.summary: Install a provider

post.description: Created suspended. Activation is separate, so a binding cannot go live before someone has confirmed it points at the intended restaurant.
post.summary: Bind an installation to a brand or location

post.description: Refused until the installation has passed a connection check.
post.summary: Activate a binding

post.description: The rollback path: operations return to a manual process while mappings and evidence are retained for reconciliation.
post.summary: Suspend a binding

post.description: Records append-only preflight evidence: the secret reference must resolve and the wired adapter must declare each capability. POS uses its specialised live discovery endpoint instead.
post.summary: Reconcile an installation's declared capabilities

get.summary: List the tenant's registered legal entities

post.description: Registered in DRAFT. A draft entity cannot be named as a seller until it is activated, so typing an INN never immediately puts it on a receipt.
post.summary: Register a company inside a tenant

get.summary: A location's fiscal-assignment history, most recent first
Get a legal entity

post.description: Only an ACTIVE entity may be named as a seller. Permitted from DRAFT or SUSPENDED.
post.summary: Activate a legal entity

post.description: Closes the location's currently open assignment, if any, at the new one's start date. Backdating is permitted; backdating over an existing assignment is refused.
post.summary: Assign a legal entity as a location's seller from a date
Start an onboarding run

get.summary: The tenant's current onboarding run

get.description: Blocked steps are listed with the decision that would unblock them, so a tenant that is live without a check is visible rather than implied.
get.summary: One onboarding run with every step

post.description: Requires every required step to have completed, plus platform approval where a policy demands it. Activating twice produces one transition.
post.summary: Activate the tenant

post.description: Completed steps are never reset; a retry reconciles external work.
post.summary: Reopen failed steps

get.description: Read with ORDER_READ rather than the manage capability, because the cancel dialog has to populate its list for every operator who can cancel an order and almost none of them may author one.
get.summary: The reasons of one kind

post.description: A cancellation reason decides the stock disposition, the liable party and the refund posture; none of the three has a safe default and all three are required. A completion reason names the fulfilment modes it is valid for, because without that «Самовывоз выполнен» lands on a delivery order and the courier SLA report quietly loses it.
post.summary: Register a reason

get.description: Closed and code-owned. Tenant registries drift into dozens of near-duplicates and that is contained rather than prevented: the category is what cross-tenant reporting groups by, and the tenant's own wording is only what the operator picks from.
get.summary: The platform categories a reason of this kind may carry

delete.description: Archived, never deleted. Outcomes recorded under it must still resolve, and the active-name uniqueness index frees the name for a replacement.

put.description: Outcomes already recorded keep the snapshot they were recorded with. That duplication is deliberate: renaming a reason next year must not rewrite last year's funnel.
put.summary: Rewrite a reason and bump its version

get.description: Exports whose outcome the platform could not establish. An empty list is the ordinary state; a growing one means a till or a network is unwell.
get.summary: Exports waiting on a decision

get.description: Provider orders that resemble this export. Resemblance is not identity: unless the provider echoed our own reference, none of these is proof.
get.summary: What the recovery read found

post.description: Side-effect free. It searches the provider and attaches what it found; it never re-sends the order.
post.summary: Read the provider to find out what happened

post.description: LANDED requires the provider order it landed as, because everything downstream — the fiscal write-back, the reconciliation — keys on it. ABSENT permits one further export attempt. ABANDON does not.
post.summary: Settle an export a person had to decide

post.description: Reads the provider, stages a snapshot, and produces a difference report. It stops there: nothing in this call changes a menu.
post.summary: Start a catalog import

post.description: Probes the provider with this restaurant's own credential. Capability varies per installation because the credential acts as a staff user the restaurant chose, so this is discovery and not a lookup.
post.summary: Rediscover what an installation can do

get.description: Deterministic: re-running the comparison over the same snapshot produces this list again, in this order.
get.summary: The difference report

get.description: Archived channels are listed because a historical order still renders through one; the status says whether a new cart may use it.
get.summary: List a tenant's sales channels, archived ones included

post.description: The system type comes from a closed, code-owned list. A tenant may run several channels of one type — Uzum Tezkor and Yandex Eda are both AGGREGATOR and must differ in price plane, payment mix, and reporting.
post.summary: Register a sales channel

post.description: Channels archive and never delete. Every order carries its channel forever, and a deleted row makes that order unattributable in every report.
post.summary: Archive a channel

put.description: Dine-in is a mode here and never a channel: a QR-table order and a waiter-entered order are both DINE_IN on different channels.
put.summary: Replace the channel's fulfilment-mode matrix

put.description: A location absent from the set is not served by the channel; the resolver returns CHANNEL_NOT_ENABLED rather than falling through to hours.
put.summary: Replace the set of locations selling on this channel

get.summary: The channel's payment, fulfilment, and location matrices

put.description: Whole matrix, never per cell: a matrix edited cell by cell from two tabs produces a combination neither operator chose.
put.summary: Replace the channel's payment-method matrix

get.summary: The tenant's live subscription

get.description: Measured and adjusted quantities stay apart. A single consumed total cannot answer how much of a figure a person decided, and that is the first question asked about a disputed one.
get.summary: Metered usage per key and period
